# Temple Scroll Column 51 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 51 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**51:1** If you see your brother's ox or sheep wandering off, do not look the other way; you must make sure to bring them back to your brother.

**51:2** And if your brother does not live nearby, or you do not know whose animal it is, bring it home with you and keep it until your brother comes looking for it, then give it back to him.

**51:3** Do the same with his donkey, his cloak, or anything else your brother has lost that you happen to find; you must not turn a blind eye.

**51:4** If you see your brother's donkey or ox collapsed on the road, do not look away; you must help him get the animal back on its feet.

**51:5** A woman must not wear what belongs to a man, and a man must not put on a woman's clothing, for anyone who does this is detestable to the LORD your God.

**51:6** If you come across a bird's nest along the road, whether in a tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs and the mother bird sitting on them, do not take the mother along with the young.

**51:7** Let the mother go free, but you may take the young for yourself, so that things will go well for you and you will enjoy a long life.

**51:8** When you build a new house, put a railing around the edge of your roof, so that you will not be guilty of bloodshed if someone falls from it.

**51:9** Do not plant two different kinds of seed in your vineyard, or the entire crop will be ruined — both the seed you planted and the fruit of your vineyard.

**51:10** Do not plow with an ox and a donkey harnessed together.

**51:11** Do not wear clothing woven from two different materials, such as wool and linen together.

**51:12** Make tassels on the four corners of the outer garment you wear.

**51:13** Suppose a man marries a woman, sleeps with her, and then turns against her,

**51:14** and makes accusations against her and publicly shames her, saying: I married this woman, but when I slept with her I discovered she was not a virgin —

**51:15** then the young woman's father and mother must bring proof of her virginity to the elders of the city at the town gate.

**51:16** The young woman's father must say to the elders: I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, and now he has turned against her.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 51 presents Deuteronomy 22:1-17 recast as God's direct speech. Language has been made accessible while preserving the legal force of each command. "Proof of virginity" for betulim conveys the legal function of the evidence. "Railing" for ma'aqeh communicates the safety purpose more immediately than "parapet."*
